Hey Rich, 

Honestly, I'm confused..  

I think i understand the basis of being caution for onboarding someone new. Concerns about dedication, commitment and work ethic. I've began contributing since February. For the last 3 months, I've worked through sickness, family emergencies and even a passing. I've continued to build a reputation.     

And to answer the question directly, Yes. This isn't a precedent, please see our most recent onboarding in April.

Thinking this over, I do wonder if this is a little on the high side [@ZOMBII](/edgeware/account/jYv1mozd5KbFGabpj9btRk6PhqoDpoASXhzsCgzc2QQXPHE) - not sure we've had anyone go from nothing to a relatively high salary this quick, just worth considering if there's maybe an intermediate stage?
one other thing i'd add is maybe some better curation / updates on proposals going into vote - basically we need to keep reminding people to vote.

Hey Rich!, Thanks for the feedback... replies below


Few thoughts working through:
> **NSP: **Shankar Warang, Edgeware Agency
Great to see another [NSP](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/3650-decent-partners-an-introduction-to-network-services), just for clarity, are you saying Edgeware Agency is the NSP, with you doing the work?


Yes, Shankar is from the Agency. 


> **Incentives**
Nicely broken down, its nice to see how Zovern has contributed first, then asked for funding after building trust / connections and understanding the gaps that need to be filled.
_Total in USD: $ 7407.4 per month_
_Non-incentivized contribution months: March & April 2022_
Are we agreeing the contract for one month or ongoing?
How are you tackling the monthly re-price needed for $$$ payments?
This is a challenge we all face - and maybe worth us developing as a task with Rusty Crew Mates - the way to approve a single 6 month salary, that automatically reprices from an oracle and executes a transaction end of each month, to ensure consistent monthly income in fiat.
What do you think [@Ramsey](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) ?
 
Yes is ongoing. Shankar drafted it to become part of the SCU monthly distribution.
Yes i Rust Crew's pallet post and I'm always eager to integrate our advancements throughout the chains. This might help to streamline the funding for the support groups. Currently, I believe the support teams (Agency/ SCU) are  annually and semi-annual funded through proposals. 

(Part1)
Final question and this is now about rates - how did you get to: $ 52.91/hour
My thinking is evolving with the structure of core member salaries... I'm wondering if we keep things simple and create a very easy to understand remuneration format:
Example:
Starter - £2500 per month
Mid - £5000 per month
Senior - £7500 per month
Core - £10,000 per month


oh, It was based hours. I'm actually committing over 45+ weekly. I lowered the rate in consideration to something more appropriate to salary. Being from corporate, I understand the demand for required will never match actual time. It's about success.

Part2
I think we can develop this idea a bit, I know others will disagree, but I see no reason why anyone needs a 'basic' above £10,000 per month.
We need to develop a basic structure, rather than everyone just creating another initial payment structure.

There are ways to bonus this / add incentives on top, but I think it'd be worth formalising something like this.
Currently [@Thom Ivy](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) is the 'best paid' in the community, I haven't taken a salary despite it being my sole job - though will be putting in a proposal for my time to date and ongoing and [@Ramsey](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) is still working on project fee, but when he moves to being an NSP, i think that would mean he also assumes a 'core' role in the community and accesses the 'benefit' of a stable salary.

Clearly, i'm aligned and I think Tiers work great toward a framework for benchmarking. I caution if it applied to stringently though.  They are those in Technology (Networking & Security) earning closer to 200K annually, based purely on their proficiency and experience.  Limiting the on-boarding structure, may also impact the level of contribution available to our chains. ( EDG & KAB )


Currently [@Thom Ivy](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) is the 'best paid' in the community, I haven't taken a salary despite it being my sole job - though will be putting in a proposal for my time to date and ongoing and [@Ramsey](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) is still working on project fee, but when he moves to being an NSP, i think that would mean he also assumes a 'core' role in the community and accesses the 'benefit' of a stable salary.


Yes, as I understand ( from previous posts) Decent Partners receives an NSP amount for contribution. I wondered why not a salary, I understand the value of creating a structure. Would help streamling onboarding and would help to highlight the contributions of a core citizen such as Ramsey. The rate, again is something I'll avoid being stringent.


-I've hired about 20+ employees and learned that baselines are great guidelines for clearly defined roles.  Here i feel, most contributions are unique as the citizens contributing.

Great to see.

Few thoughts working through:

> **NSP: **Shankar Warang, Edgeware Agency 

Great to see another [NSP](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/3650-decent-partners-an-introduction-to-network-services),  just for clarity, are you saying Edgeware Agency is the NSP, with you doing the work?

> **Incentives**

Nicely broken down, its nice to see how Zovern has contributed first, then asked for funding after building trust / connections and understanding the gaps that need to be filled.

	_Total in USD: $ 7407.4 per month _
_	Non-incentivized contribution months: March & April 2022 _

Are we agreeing the contract for one month or ongoing?
How are you tackling the monthly re-price needed for $$$ payments? 

This is a challenge we all face - and maybe worth us developing as a task with Rusty Crew Mates - the way to approve a single 6 month salary, that automatically reprices from an oracle and executes a transaction end of each month, to ensure consistent monthly income in fiat.

What do you think [@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) ? 

Final question and this is now about rates - how did you get to: $ 52.91/hour 

My thinking is evolving with the structure of core member salaries... I'm wondering if we keep things simple and create a very easy to understand remuneration format:

Example:

Starter - £2500 per month
Mid - £5000 per month
Senior - £7500 per month
Core - £10,000 per month

I think we can develop this idea a bit, I know others will disagree, but I see no reason why anyone needs a 'basic' above £10,000 per month.

We need to develop a basic structure, rather than everyone just creating another initial payment structure.

There are ways to bonus this / add incentives on top, but I think it'd be worth formalising something like this. 

Currently [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) is the 'best paid' in the community, I haven't taken a salary despite it being my sole job -
